# Neon Monkey Tree Service — Call Wins Log

Day-by-day log of every CallRail-recorded call that's ad-generated (Google Ads Call Extension, the Website-pool tracking number, Google Local Services Ads, or Google My Business — matched by source or by a gclid on the call), 2026-10-01 through 2026-10-15. 34 calls total. Each one was transcribed locally with faster-whisper (no cloud ASR) and cross-checked against CallRail's own call metadata.

**Caveat:** names, cities, and spelled-out details come from an auto-generated transcript on phone-quality audio, plus CallRail's own caller-ID lookup — both can be wrong. Where the transcript and CallRail's metadata clearly disagree (a different name, a different city), both are noted. Treat this as a leads list to verify against the office's own records, not a verified one.

**Outcome legend:** ✅ Booked · ⏳ Open/follow-up needed · ❌ Not a lead · ⚠️ IVR-only (never reached a live person)

## Running tally (2026-10-01 → 2026-10-15, 34 calls)

| Outcome | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ Booked | 0 | No appointment is confirmed as scheduled on any call in this set — every live new lead ends with "Kip will call you within the hour," never a set day/time on the recording itself. Check Kip's calendar / the job system to see how many of these actually turned into booked jobs. |
| ⏳ Open | 11 (10 unique leads; one call is a duplicate add-on to another) | Stephanie Anz (10-01, senior discount), Amjad Ali (10-05, later cancelled 10-06), Homer Corn (10-07, existing customer, city compliance trim), Patsy Weaver (10-08, two calls = one lead), Kathy Clark (10-12, existing customer), Cheryl Wilson (10-13, 22-min call), Tommy Carver (10-13, urgent — falling limbs), Charlie Winkley (10-14, referral), Barrett Small (10-14), Sandy Murphy (10-15, existing-customer poison-ivy retreatment) |
| ❌ Not a lead | 12 | 2 cancellations of visits that had already been booked (Amjad Ali 10-06, Sharon Bowman 10-10), 1 silent/one-word disconnect, 2 wrong numbers, 2 wrong-company mixups (Tree Shepherd, Blue Ox), 1 not-a-fit call (tree nursery confusion), 1 landscaping-rocks ask, 1 city official asking for Kip, 1 likely lost over the $500 minimum, 1 unsolicited compliment about the crew (Declan) with no service ask |
| ⚠️ IVR-only | 11 | Automated menu loops, after-hours greetings, or the self-service directory — zero live conversation on any of these, roughly a third of all 34 calls |

**Flag for Edu:** The honest read here is mixed-to-concerning, not a clean win. Zero calls in this set show a confirmed booking — every real lead gets handed off to Kip for a callback "within the hour," and the recordings simply don't show whether that callback or booking ever happens; that's a visibility gap worth closing (pull Kip's calendar or the job system against these 10 open leads to see what actually converted). 11 of 34 calls (about a third) never get past the IVR menu, after-hours greeting, or the self-service directory at all — that's real ad spend buying a dial tone, not a conversation, and it's worth checking whether the IVR flow itself is too slow or confusing. Within the "not a lead" bucket, 2 are outright cancellations of jobs that had already been scheduled, which is a different and more costly problem than a wrong number — those were real booked revenue that fell through. On the positive side: the reps (Brock, Ricardo, Rob) handled every real call professionally, including a rambling 22-minute call from Cheryl Wilson that could easily have been cut short, and the crew got an unprompted compliment from a neighbor for cleaning up a job site unasked — a good review opportunity if it's followed up on. Bottom line: lead flow and call handling both look fine, but the complete lack of visible bookings plus the IVR drop-off rate are the two things worth pushing on.

*Oct 16–20 calls added 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-20 (day sections above); the tally table covers Oct 1–15.*
